# Stepper
Atlas Stepper — numbered markers joined by connectors, showing where someone is in a multi-step flow. Orientation × Size × Steps × Current (72 total).

USE WHEN
· A flow with a known, small number of steps (onboarding, checkout, setup) where each step has a name.
· Showing which steps are done, which is current and which are still to come.
DON'T USE WHEN
· Only a percentage or a single task bar is needed → Progress.
· Moving between sibling views the user can open in any order → Tabs.
· Page-by-page navigation of a long list → Pagination.
HOW TO USE
· Set the steps (label and optional description) and the current step; each step's status (complete, current, upcoming) follows from it. Steps is a value in code: any count from 2 up, Figma draws 3 to 5.
· Horizontal for a header; vertical for checklists and long flows. Size sm, md or lg follows the Step Marker size.
· Name it with aria-label; the current step carries aria-current="step" and every status is also written for assistive technology.
· It shows progress only: the page controls moving between steps with Back and Continue. Markers are not buttons.
DO
· Keep labels to one or two words.
DON'T
· Use it for a flow whose length is unknown.
· Put actions on the markers.
RELATED
· Progress — a bar for how far, Stepper for which step.
· Tabs — switch between views; Stepper is read-only progress.
